A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 22 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. The methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary results can be matched reliably despite editorial changes and removal of a duplicate figure.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on MNIST variants, molecular-property prediction, and phenomics, together with calibration and stopping-criterion evaluations in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark learning curves, acquisition analyses, and repeated-trial stopping evaluations in the appendices.

M1.justification: The confidence-based acquisition procedure, residual MLP models, stopping criterion, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The regression QBC procedure remains in Appendix E.1; its explanatory paragraph moves before the figure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate original, cropped, and label-shuffled MNIST; QM9 classification; Molecules3D gap and energy regression; and RxRx3 and proprietary phenomics classification. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator membership: LC/random on MNIST, the existing LC/BALD/random and heuristic/diversity comparisons on QM9 and phenomics, and QBC/random/SA-score/molecule-size orderings on Molecules3D.

E3.justification: Splits, acquisition batches, training budgets, model sizes, metrics, and preprocessing procedures remain unchanged in Sections 4 and Appendices C–E. Calling the MNIST pool the target set and stating the existing 98% target in Figure 2 clarify the setup without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: The label-noise sweep, hard-example acquisition analyses, chemical-element coverage analysis, calibration checks, and stopping validation are retained. Removed v2 Figure 9 duplicates the QM9 calibration row already present in Appendix F.1 and retained in v3 Figure 12.

E5.justification: Both report three-seed means with standard errors, stopping-time min–max ranges, and Appendix F.2 validation across 100 seeds for MNIST variants/QM9 and 50 for phenomics. v3's 'unless specified otherwise' clarifies exceptions already documented in v2; no run counts or uncertainty practices change.

E6.justification: Matched figures retain the same curves, numerical results, and findings. Figure 8 still reports 98% system accuracy after approximately 80% acquisition. Molecules3D QBC savings remain 21.3% for gap prediction and 20.2% for energy prediction in v2 Figure 10/v3 Figure 9.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, the weak-calibration assumption, and the proofs and bound derivation in Appendix A retain their mathematical content. Reordering the lower index from 1 + N_b to N_b + 1 is equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the claims that inference set design reduces acquisition costs for finite target sets and supports a probabilistic stopping criterion under weak calibration. Wording changes do not substantively alter these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 removes the explicit explanation that SMILES omits 3D positional information and thereby makes conformation-dependent property prediction harder. The principal interpretations and limitations concerning weak calibration, low-data RxRx3 performance, and noisy experimental labels remain.

D1.justification: v2 promises code release upon publication; v3 provides a repository address and states that code is available in the Section 4 footnote. Appendix C.1 newly identifies Molfeat alongside RDKit, documenting tooling without establishing that the underlying preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Molfeat software citation, Noutahi et al. (2023), in Appendix C.1 and the references. Positioning relative to Bayesian optimization, pool-based active learning, and core-set selection remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Copyediting and local paragraph rewrites clarify the introduction and experimental descriptions, correct terminology, and remove grammatical errors. The classification-scope note moves to a footnote, and Appendix E.1 places its regression explanation before the plot. The overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The duplicate main-text calibration figure is removed while its evidence remains in Appendix F.1. Table 1 moves onto the preprocessing page, Table 2 is reformatted, and captions, spacing, and publication headers receive limited updates. Remaining figures are retained with subsequent renumbering.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future code-release promise with a concrete repository address, identifying Molfeat, and improving prose and table readability modestly improve reproducibility guidance and presentation. The scientific evidence and proofs are preserved, including the duplicated calibration results. These gains outweigh the limited loss of the explanatory discussion about SMILES and 3D information.
